title: MOPED: Efficient Motion Planning Engine with Flexible Dimension Support
problem: Sampling-based motion planning is computationally intensive due to costly kernel operations and inherent sequential processing, limiting real-time deployment across varying dimensional configuration spaces.
motivation: Efficient motion planning accelerators enable real-time robotic trajectory computation with collision avoidance in high-dimensional spaces.
method: MOPED uses a two-stage processing scheme to reduce collision check frequency and unit cost, and exploits spatial information for low-cost approximated neighbor search. At the hardware level, it employs correctness-ensured speculative processing to eliminate serialization bottlenecks and implements multi-level caching to reduce data movement and resource conflicts.
key_novelty: Algorithm-hardware co-design combining two-stage collision filtering with speculative execution to enable efficient sampling-based motion planning across flexible dimensions.
contributions: Two-stage collision check processing reducing frequency and unit cost
Approximated neighbor search leveraging spatial properties and planning process characteristics
Correctness-ensured speculative processing to overcome serialization
Multi-level caching strategy for data movement reduction and resource conflict resolution

metrics.speedup: Significant improvement vs baseline motion planning processors

limitations: Specific limitations not discussed in abstract.
